Using the product rule for natural logarithms, we can combine the first two terms of the given expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(y)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the quotient rule for natural logarithms, we get

$$
\ln(2x)-\ln(y) = \ln \left( \dfrac{2x}{y} \right).
$$

Therefore,

$$
\ln(2)+\ln(x)-\ln(y) = \ln\left(\dfrac{2x}{y}\right).
$$

- ${log}_{n}⁡(a)-{log}_{n}⁡(b)={log}_{n}⁡\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)$ - the quotient rule

- ${log}_{n}⁡({c}^{m})=m{log}_{n}⁡(c)$ - the power rule

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡\left(\frac{ex}{5}\right) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(ex)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\  & =1+\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(5).\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quotient rule and then the product rule for logarithms, we have

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Express $\ln\left(q\right)-\ln\left(p\right)-\ln\left(9\right)$ as a single logarithm. Assume $q>0$ and $p>0$.
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Using the product rule, combine the logarithms with the same sign. Then use the quotient rule to subtract the denominator logarithm:

$$
\begin{aligned}\ln\left(q\right)-\ln\left(p\right)-\ln\left(9\right) &= \ln\left(q\right)-\ln\left(p\cdot 9\right) \\ &= \ln\left(\frac{q}{9\cdot p}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Express $-\ln\left(5\right)-\ln\left(z\right)+\ln\left(x\right)$ as a single logarithm. Assume $x>0$ and $z>0$.
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Using the product rule, combine the logarithms with the same sign. Then use the quotient rule to subtract the denominator logarithm:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\ln\left(5\right)-\ln\left(z\right)+\ln\left(x\right) &= \ln\left(x\right)-\ln\left(5\cdot z\right) \\ &= \ln\left(\frac{x}{5\cdot z}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Express $\log\left(9\right)+\log\left(z\right)-\log\left(x\right)$ as a single logarithm. Assume $z>0$ and $x>0$.
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Using the product rule, combine the logarithms with the same sign. Then use the quotient rule to subtract the denominator logarithm:

$$
\begin{aligned}\log\left(9\right)+\log\left(z\right)-\log\left(x\right) &= \log\left(9\cdot z\right)-\log\left(x\right) \\ &= \log\left(\frac{9\cdot z}{x}\right).\end{aligned}
$$
